To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

‘unresolved inflammation’ is a term coined to describe loss of balance between ‘tumoricidal versus tumorigenic’ properties of innate immune system that cause disruption of immunological barriers in immune-privileged or immune-responsive tissues and cause inflammatory or vascular diseases or cancer.

‘immune tsunami’ refers to the loss of balance between the two biologically opposing processes that are otherwise essential for protection of tissues and organs from infections, cancer and other diseases.

‘immune tsunami’ is an end result of acute or chronic inflammation-induced erosion of integrity in tissues or organs, and that ‘immune meltdown’ describes the end results of age-induced loss of integrity in immune-responsive tissues or organs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of immune system in aging process and the development of age-related diseases, including inflammatory and vascular diseases and cancer.
understanding the molecular basis of ‘immune tsunami’ and its end results, ‘immune meltdown’ in acute and chronic inflammatory and cancerous conditions.
understanding mechanisms of acute and chronic inflammatory processes, their end results and how to control them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
unresolved inflammation is a fundamental process in development of acute and chronic inflammatory or cancer diseases.

unresolved inflammation is a major cause of age-associated diseases including cancer, and that the key to preventing these diseases would lie in the ability of the immune system to maintain its integrity and to prevent excessive and prolonged expression of inflammatory mediators that would otherwise lead to ‘immune tsunami’ (‘immune meltdown’).
unresolved inflammation is the end result of loss of immune balance in tissues that are immune-responsive or immune-privileged.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to understand and control inflammation-induced tissue damage, we must understand the role of apoptotic mediators and how they influence immune system integrity.
‘immune tsunami’ is the end results of unresolved inflammation and loss of integrity of tissues that are either naturally immune-responsive or immune-privileged.
the ‘tumoricidal versus tumorigenic’ properties of innate immune system are the basis for immune-privileged and responsive tissues and their integrity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune response is a double-edged sword.

the immune system is designed for self-defense against pathogens, but it also can be a major contributor to disease development, and that immune dysfunction is an underlying cause of multiple diseases including cancer, inflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases, and aging.
the ‘immune tsunami’ hypothesis may be applicable in a wide variety of inflammatory conditions and diseases.
